title: Tool Call Fidelity Migration and Resume Playbook
content:
Purpose

This is a working playbook for migrating client and hosted-api integrations across graded output fidelities while preserving safe tool-calling semantics and resumability for long-running or intermittent connections. The emphasis: predictable developer ergonomics + clear rollback/fallback during fidelity downgrades or model variant switches.

Background/problem statement

We ship model variants and runtime fallbacks that produce different structured outputs: from rich typed JSON (high-fidelity) to terse tokenized frames or plain text (low-fidelity). Customers integrate tool-calls (webhook triggers, DB ops, 3rd-party APIs) against the contract we return. When we change model variant or downgrade fidelity at runtime (cost spikes, capacity constraints, or safety fallback), clients can receive messages with different shape/granularity. This currently causes brittle client logic, partial-action duplication, and complicated resume semantics when streams disconnect.

Goals
- Define lightweight protocol guarantees that let clients: detect fidelity level, safely decide whether to execute a tool call, and resume partially-completed sessions without duplicating side effects.
- Provide SDK ergonomics that minimize client-side plumbing (idempotency, commit checkpoints, and backpressure-aware buffering).
- Create a stepwise rollout plan for migrating hosted API from always-high-fidelity toward adaptive-fidelity routing under load.

Non-goals
- This doc does not prescribe exact wire format bytes; we'll iterate on a compact framing draft in a follow-up.
- This is not a spec for server-side model selection policies (routing heuristics live in another doc), but we include necessary hooks.

Key constraints and assumptions
- Clients may be mobile, server, or edge. Network disconnects are common.
- Tool calls must be at-least-once safe by default; we prefer explicit idempotency tokens to avoid duplication.
- Streaming SDKs will provide a small, stable surface — open to language idioms but consistent semantics.
- Rollouts must be reversible with deterministic client fallback behaviors.

Terminology
- Fidelity level: high | medium | low (human-friendly shorthand). High = typed structured output with tool call objects. Medium = compact frames with minimal metadata. Low = plain text with markup hints or markers.
- Commit checkpoint: server-provided token that marks safe-to-run tool-calls up to that point.
- Execution ticket: client-generated idempotency token for a tool-call (client or server generated — prefer client for visibility).

Developer scenarios (user stories)
- U1: Server-side assistant uses Hosted API to call a payment service. It must not charge twice if the stream reconnects.
- U2: Mobile note-taking app receives partial summaries during intermittent connectivity; app should resume and patch UI without re-triggering external webhooks.
- U3: SRE tool uses thin-client to fan out tool-calls; operator wants confidence that fidelity downgrade due to capacity will not drop critical metadata.

Protocol-level guarantees (consumer-facing)
- Fidelity indicator header: every response frame includes a "fidelity" field: one of [high, medium, low]. SDKs expose this as an enum.
- Checkpoint markers: streaming frames MAY include a checkpoint token (opaque string). A checkpoint indicates that any tool-calls that appear in prior frames are durable and safe to execute.
- Idempotency tokens: every tool-call structure SHOULD include an "exec_ticket" (client-provided or generated by SDK). Server logs exec_ticket and includes it in any repeated frames.
- Execution preflight: clients can request a preflight acknowledgement mode where the server returns a "preflight-ok" for a tool-call (useful for synchronous mode).

Behavior rules by fidelity level
- High fidelity: frames include structured tool_call objects with {name, args (typed), exec_ticket, commit_checkpoint?}. SDK default: auto-ack only once commit_checkpoint is seen; option to auto-execute earlier with warning.
- Medium fidelity: frames contain condensed frames: action-id + payload blob + maybe partial schema. SDK exposes a typed parser helper but requires explicit parse call before execution. Commit checkpoints are more frequent to compensate for coarser frames.
- Low fidelity: plain text. SDK offers best-effort autoframe extraction heuristic + safe sandboxed preview that requires manual confirmation before executing tool-calls.

SDK ergonomics (defaults and opt-ins)
- Default mode: conservative (never auto-execute tool-calls until commit checkpoint). Rationale: minimise accidental external side-effects for new adopters.
- Convenience opt-in: "eager-execute" flag for power users; SDK will attempt to parse and run tool-calls as they appear, but still include dedupe by exec_ticket.
- Resumability primitives: SDKs persist last-seen checkpoint and outstanding exec_ticket states in a small local store (in-memory for ephemeral, disk for durable clients). On reconnect, SDK asks server for delta since checkpoint.
- Backpressure: SDK tracks inflight parsing+execution queue length; if queue exceeds threshold, it signals upstream with a small "waterline" token suggesting throttle (server may delay or downgrade fidelity).

Resume and deduplication flow (example)
1) Client opens stream, sends session_id and optionally last_checkpoint.
2) Server streams frames, some include tool_call objects with exec_ticket T1.
3) Client buffers tool_call until it sees checkpoint C1 in a later frame.
4) On seeing C1, SDK marks exec_ticket T1 as committed and executes the call (or hands exec_ticket to client's tool-runner). Execution logs include exec_ticket.
5) If connection drops before C1, client reconnects and sends last_checkpoint (null). Server repeats frames starting before T1 but includes exec_ticket T1; SDK sees T1 as outstanding but not committed and will not re-execute. If server had already committed T1 (server side stores), it may include a server-side 'committed: true' flag; SDK then marks as executed.

Safety boundaries and migration behavior
- If fidelity is downgraded mid-session, server MUST include a "fidelity-change" frame explaining reason (capacity|safety|cost) and recommended client mode (conservative|eager-preview). SDK surfaces this to app telemetry and exposes a callback for product UX (e.g., show "low-fidelity mode" banner).
- For tool-calls that require sensitive args, high-fidelity is required by default; server will not downgrade such frames to low-fidelity. Policy: any tool-call tagged "P0-sensitive" cannot be downgraded unless an explicit customer setting permits lossy fallback.

Observability and alerts
- Telemetry events: fidelity_change, checkpoint_emitted, exec_ticket_committed, exec_ticket_executed, exec_ticket_deduped. Include session_id, model_variant, and region.
- Rollout alert rule: if >0.5% of sessions see fidelity change within first minute after connecting, send a channel alert (product + SRE) — indicates too-aggressive routing.

Migration & rollout plan (high-level)
- Phase 0 (lab): internal SDK + QA harness test of exec_ticket flows across synthetic disconnects.
- Phase 1 (beta customers): opt-in for a small set of customers with non-sensitive tool-calls; gather telemetry.
- Phase 2 (gradual routing): enable adaptive-fidelity for 5% of traffic with clear rollback toggles.
- Phase 3 (wide): default to adaptive-fidelity with conservative SDK defaults and migration documentation.

Open questions / decisions needed
- Should exec_ticket be server-assigned instead of client-provided for stronger server-side auditability? Pros/cons: server-assigned centralizes control but complicates dedupe across reconnects.
- Exact format and length of checkpoint tokens — opaque vs structured.
- Backpressure API shape: header vs in-stream frame.
- How to surface fidelity changes in existing minimal REST endpoints (non-streaming)?

Next steps / action items
- (Eng) PoC streaming shim that inserts checkpoint tokens and verifies exec_ticket dedupe (JIRA-API-4821) — owner: Ethan — due 2025-02-26.
- (Product) Finalize list of tool-call tags that block fidelity downgrade (Priya) — due 2025-03-05.
- (SDK) Add resume primitives and local checkpoint store to node/python sdks; default conservative mode — owner: Marta — due 2025-03-12.
- (Docs) Draft migration guide and sample integrations for serverless payment and webhook patterns — owner: Jordan — due 2025-03-12.

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally pragmatic. We prioritized simple semantics that fit our current streaming pipeline. Expect follow-ups that tighten framing and wire formats. Please comment with specific developer UX concerns — especially mobile/resume cases and serverless idempotency patterns.

Rough appendix: short example frames (informal)
- high fidelity frame: {fidelity: "high", frame_type: "tool_call", exec_ticket: "T-abc-01", tool: "charge-card", args: {amount: 1500, currency: "USD"}}
- checkpoint frame: {fidelity: "high", frame_type: "checkpoint", checkpoint: "C-20250212-01"}
- fidelity-change frame: {fidelity: "medium", frame_type: "meta", change_reason: "capacity", recommended_mode: "conservative"}

-- end of draft playbook --
